title: Structural Optimization
description: A lattice pavilion structure evaluated through shell analysis, catenary form-finding and beam optimization for 3D-printable fabrication.
body: Tunnel Pavilion investigates the design and evaluation of a lattice structure using computational geometry and structural optimization. The workflow begins with a shell analysis to understand stress distribution and deflection behaviour, which then guides the lattice design.

The structure is converted into a lattice system and analysed under self-weight and wind loads using recycled reinforced-glass beam elements, with lattice topologies compared for both structural performance and fabrication efficiency.

sections.title: Workflow
body: Three stages, each feeding the next: the surface is explored parametrically, analysed as a continuous shell, then converted into a lattice and optimized as a beam system.

sections.title: Geometry Exploration
body: The geometry originates from a parametric surface equation. Adjusting scale factor, pinch strength and wave amplitude produces multiple design variations, and the surface is then reshaped by catenary curves.

scenes.title: Surface
scenes.caption: The base surface in plan and elevation — 8 m span, rising to a maximum height of 5.4 m.

scenes.title: Parametric Surface Equation
scenes.caption: Variations generated by adjusting scale factor, pinch strength and wave amplitude in the surface equation.

scenes.title: Catenary Curves
scenes.caption: The same surface reshaped along catenary curves, trading a small increase in deflection for lower stress.

sections.title: Shell Analysis
body: The shell was analysed in two options — the original mesh, and one formed from the catenary curves. Remeshing strategy matters here: guiding the QuadRemesh along the curves aligns the faces with the structural direction.

scenes.title: Stress Lines
scenes.caption: Principal stress lines across the shell, the field the lattice is later aligned to.

scenes.title: Remeshing
scenes.caption: QuadRemesh on its own against QuadRemesh guided by the stress curves.

scenes.title: Deflection and Stress
scenes.caption: Deflection peaking at 0.66 mm and von Mises stress at 0.68 MPa across the continuous shell.

sections.title: Lattice Structure Analysis
body: Among the lattice configurations generated with the Crystallon plug-in, StarTet and BC Cubic gave the best balance of structural performance and fabrication efficiency, needing the fewest total beam elements — which matters directly for 3D printing. Further optimization explored variable lattice thickness and beam sizing.
